w: A 2,590m peak above Davos Platz, reached by a two-part cable car and served by chairlifts and a T-bar higher up. Fourteen pistes make it one of five Davos ski areas, prized by snowboarders for Bolgen's illuminated super pipe and by paragliders and snowkiters. Lifts also run July-October for summer walkers.
s: Cable car peak famed for its floodlit snowboard pipe
_facts: 2,590m peak of the Albula Alps served by a two-part cable car from Davos Platz
Fourteen pistes; renowned snowboarding centre with Bolgen's illuminated super pipe
Popular with hang-gliders and snowkiters
Main lifts also open in summer (July-October) for walkers

w: A natural lake of 0.59 sq km and 54m depth, fed by headwaters of the Rhine along with the Fluelabach and Totalpbach creeks. Its outflow no longer follows the historic route to the river Landwasser; instead the lake is dammed as a hydropower reservoir and channeled into the Landquart at Klosters.
s: Natural lake doubling as a hydropower reservoir
_facts: 0.59 sq km surface area, maximum depth 54m
Fed by Rhine headwaters, Fluelabach and Totalpbach creeks
Used as a hydropower reservoir
Water now diverted to the Landquart at Klosters, not the Landwasser

w: A former hi-tech tuberculosis sanatorium at 1,860m, reached only by the Schatzalp-Bahn funicular below. A Cultural Property of National Significance, it reopened as the Berghotel Schatzalp in 1953. Each January, during the World Economic Forum, the Telegraph calls it the fashionable party address in town.
s: Former TB sanatorium reached only by funicular
_facts: Art Nouveau former tuberculosis sanatorium at 1,860m
Cultural Property of National Significance
Reached only by the Schatzalp-Bahn funicular from Davos
Reopened as Berghotel Schatzalp in 1953; hosts private WEF parties each January

w: A 2,843m summit of the Plessur Alps above Davos, part of a linked ski area, its top reached by cable car climbing from the Weissfluhjoch below. The final stage in a chain of lifts out of the valley floor, it draws skiers up for the descent and hikers for the ridge views across the Graubunden peaks.
s: Summit above the Parsenn ski area, reached by cable car
_facts: 2,843m summit of the Plessur Alps above Davos
Summit served by cable car from the Weissfluhjoch
Part of a linked ski area

w: A 2,693m summit reached since 1932 by the Parsennbahn funicular from Davos, one of the earliest mountain railways in the region. It once housed laboratories of the Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research; a test site remains today, though the institute's own building was sold to Davos Klosters Bergbahnen in 2019.
s: Funicular summit that once housed avalanche scientists
_facts: 2,693m summit above Davos, southeast of Weissfluh (2,843m)
Reached since 1932 by the Parsennbahn funicular
Former home of the Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research (WSL)
Institute building sold to Davos Klosters Bergbahnen in 2019; test site remains

w: Opened in 1969 and expanded three times since, in 1979, 1989 and 2010, this is the hall that has hosted the World Economic Forum's annual meeting every January since 1971. It is the reason Davos becomes, for one week a year, a byword for global finance and politics rather than for skiing.
s: The hall where the World Economic Forum meets each January
_facts: Opened 1969; major extensions in 1979, 1989 and 2010
Has hosted the WEF annual meeting since 1971

w: Devoted entirely to Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, the German Expressionist painter who settled in Davos in 1918 and remained there until 1938. The Alpine landscape and light around the town inspired many of the works gathered here, tracing two decades of a major twentieth-century artist's mountain years under one roof.
s: Museum devoted to Expressionist Kirchner's mountain years
_facts: Sole museum dedicated to Ernst Ludwig Kirchner
Kirchner lived in Davos 1918-1938
Many works created there were inspired by the Davos landscape

w: At 1,632m, this pass links Klosters and Davos, with Davos almost level with the summit. A Rhaetian Railway line has crossed it since 1890, and its road once carried trade toward the Scaletta Pass and later the Flueela Pass, which still closes each winter, forcing motorists onto the Vereina Tunnel car-shuttle train.
s: Low pass linking Klosters and Davos since 1890
_facts: 1,632m pass connecting Klosters and Davos
Rhaetian Railway line has crossed it since 1890
Historically used for trade via the Scaletta and Flueela passes
Flueela route closes in winter; traffic uses the Vereina Tunnel car-shuttle train
